question: A report shows old information after I corrected the scan — how do I refresh it?
reasons:
Substance is right, but the cited evidence does not hold up and one factual claim is wrong.

1) Both evidence line ranges are wrong. In the working tree `server/app.js`, `function buildScanReport(rackId, { inlineImages = true } = {})` is at line 1375 (cited 1343-1350; lines 1343-1350 are the CSV port-console transcript loop in `renderCSVReport`). `app.post('/api/scan/:rackId/report', ...)` starts at line 5036 (cited 5004-5017; those lines are the `format === 'json'` / `format === 'csv'` branches of the GET route). The ranges do not match the committed HEAD version either — `git show HEAD:server/app.js` at 1343 and 5004 shows the same unrelated code — so this is not just uncommitted drift. The snippet text itself is verbatim-accurate at the real locations (the only difference is the working copy has an extra comment line "// Failures are swallowed inside writeCanonicalScanResult" inside buildScanReport, which the snippet omits).

2) "Administrators can also force a rebuild" is incorrect. `POST /api/scan/:rackId/report` (line 5036) has no admin gate; authorisation comes solely from the global `app.param('rackId')` guard at line 203, which admits the owner, an org_admin whose org owns the rack, and any authenticated member of the tenant that owns the rack (and even a valid `?t=` report token). Any ordinary technician on the owning site can call it. Telling an end user this is an admin-only lever is misleading.

Verified as correct: `GET /api/scan/:rackId/report?format=html` calls `buildScanReport(rackId)` at line 4984, which rebuilds from `buildScanReportData` (line 781: re-reads `device_unit_map.json`, `port_identifications.jsonl`, `feedback.jsonl` from the rack's outputs dir) and `fs.writeFileSync(reportPath, html)` overwrites `report.html`. The client's "View" chip (`client/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx:2583`, `viewReport` at 2597, "Report row — View / Download / Share" at 3863) opens exactly that URL in an iframe, so View does regenerate. `/outputs` is served as plain static (`server/app.js:273`), so the bookmarked file only changes when someone builds a report. The POST response and `audit.log({ action: 'report.regen' })` are exactly as described.

The mechanical half checks out, but the load-bearing promise to the technician is wrong.

CONFIRMED against /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/app.js:
- buildScanReport (1375) re-reads via buildScanReportData (781): device_unit_map.json (786), port_identifications.jsonl (817), feedback.jsonl (830), then overwrites <rackDir>/report.html.
- GET /api/scan/:rackId/report?format=html (4976-4993) calls buildScanReport, so it does rewrite the on-disk file; POST /api/scan/:rackId/report (5036-5050) does the same and logs action 'report.regen'. /outputs is plain express.static (273), so the file link really is a stale snapshot.
- A **View** chip does exist (client/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx:3866-3870); viewReport (2597) opens an iframe on reportUrl('html') (2582, 4037/4897), i.e. the regenerating route.

REFUTING problems:
1. "corrections you made ... will be in it" is false for most corrections. writeCanonicalScanResult applies applyFeedbackOverrides (app.js:1434) but that runs on scan_result.json ONLY — renderHTMLReport is handed the raw buildScanReportData output with no feedback overlay. Concretely, POST /api/feedback/port-count (8258-8320) only READS device_unit_map.json to record the predicted value and never writes back, so a tech who corrects "24 ports" to "48" taps View, sees 24 again, and reasonably concludes the refresh is broken. Same for port-number corrections via POST /api/feedback (7912+), which also performs no writeback. Only device-class feedback persists (8189-8197 writes class_name / class_name_source='user_corrected' into device_unit_map.json); cable colour only re-sticks after the port is re-selected (3296-3316). Everything else surfaces only as rows in the report's Feedback section, not in the device/port tables.
2. There are no controls labelled "wrong?". The feedback widgets prompt with a trailing "— right?" plus Yes/No (e.g. ResultsPage.jsx:3602 `Port type: ... — right?`). Quoting a non-existent label sends the tech hunting.
3. Audience mismatch: tagged end-user, yet it hands a customer a raw API endpoint and an internal audit-log action name.

Directionally right on refresh mechanics, wrong on the outcome the technician actually cares about — so it misleads.

question: The user guide mentions a "Report" button that opens in a new tab, but I only see View and Share
reasons: Most of the entry checks out, but its final instruction is wrong and would waste a technician's time. VERIFIED TRUE: docs/user-guide/RackTrack-User-Guide-iPhone.md line 318 does read "| **Report** | Opens the report in a new tab, ready to save or print. |" and the cited 315-320 block matches. client/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx from line 3863 renders exactly four chips in styles.reportRow — View (3865, onClick viewReport), Share (3872), Change Device (~3924) and New Scan (3926) — with no Report chip and no CSV/JSON control. openReportForDownload (line 2600) and downloadReport (2601-2617) exist and are referenced nowhere else (grep finds only their definitions), so they are dead code. server/app.js 1245-1251 puts a "Download PDF" button in the report's sticky top bar and its handler (1265-1268) swaps format=html for format=pdf and calls window.open(url, '_blank') — a new tab. FALSE: "open /api/scan/<rack ID>/report?format=csv or ?format=json in a signed-in browser". That returns 401. app.param('rackId') (server/app.js 203-215) fails closed — it accepts only a valid ?t=<report token> for that exact rack, or a Bearer JWT read from the Authorization header via softAuthPayload (114-121). Auth is header/Bearer only; there is no session cookie, so pasting the URL into a browser tab sends no credential and yields {"error":"Authentication required"}. The comment at 4972-4974 confirms the only real JSON caller is ProfilePage via authFetch (ProfilePage.jsx:82); no client code ever requests format=csv. The same flaw is why dead downloadReport() would not have worked: it does a bare fetch(reportUrl(format)) with no Authorization header. Shipping that CSV/JSON instruction to an end user is a concrete, reproducible dead end, so the entry is refuted rather than merely imprecise.

The core of the entry checks out: docs/user-guide/RackTrack-User-Guide-iPhone.md line ~316 does list a stale "Report | Opens the report in a new tab" row, ResultsPage.jsx:3863-3930 renders exactly four chips (View, Share, Change Device, New Scan) with no Report/CSV/JSON control, openReportForDownload/downloadReport (lines 2600-2601) are confirmed dead code with zero call sites, and server/app.js:1245-1252 does put a "Download PDF" button in the report's top bar that window.open()s the format=pdf URL in a new tab. However, the final paragraph is factually wrong and would strand the technician: server/app.js:203-215 (app.param('rackId')) fails closed, and softAuthPayload() reads credentials ONLY from the Authorization: Bearer header — there is no cookie session. Opening /api/scan/<rackId>/report?format=csv in a browser, signed in or not, returns 401 {"error":"Authentication required"}. The only other path in is ?t=<report token>, minted solely by the authenticated /report-token endpoint, which no user-facing control exposes. Shipping that instruction to an end user guarantees a dead end, so the entry must be corrected before use.

question: Can I export the Operations Console audit feed or the Logs tab?
reasons:
The headline "no export exists" is true, and the retention numbers and the ACTION_LABELS gap check out. But the limits and the paging claim are attributed to the wrong surfaces and are wrong for the two views the entry names.

Confirmed true:
- No CSV/export/download control in client/src/pages/DashboardPage.jsx or client/src/pages/LogsPage.jsx; no export route in server/audit.js or server/lib/log-store.js. (A `format=csv` export does exist, but only for the per-rack scan report at server/app.js ~5008, not for audit/logs.)
- server/lib/log-store.js:35-36 — RETENTION_DAYS default 7 (LOG_RETENTION_DAYS), MAX_ROWS default 200000 (LOG_MAX_ROWS), both enforced in prune (lines 136-144).
- client/src/pages/LogsPage.jsx:251 — "Clear log" button, backed by POST /api/logs/clear (server/app.js:1852).
- ACTION_LABELS (DashboardPage.jsx:7-31) contains only 'scan.share.outlook' and 'scan.share.teams'; labelFor falls through to the raw key (line 31). 'report.regen' is logged at server/app.js:5040/5052 and 'scan.share.slack' is produced by the template literal `scan.share.${channel}` at server/app.js:7460-7532 with channel='slack' (client/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx:2556). So that gap is real.

Refuting facts:
- The Operations Console audit feed does NOT call audit.query / GET /api/audit. DashboardPage.jsx:78 fetches only `/api/admin/dashboard`, whose activity feed is a hardcoded `ORDER BY a.id DESC LIMIT 80` (server/app.js:1929-1936) with a separate errors list at `LIMIT 30`. The "100 rows by default, capped at 1000" figures are true of server/audit.js:212/249 but are irrelevant to the console view the answer describes — a reader is told 100 when they actually see 80.
- The Logs tab always requests a fixed `limit: '300'` (LogsPage.jsx:143), so the "200 rows by default" from log-store.js:197 never applies to the tab either.
- "read-only views with paging" is invented. Neither view has any paging/offset/load-more control (no `offset`, `page`, or "Load more" in DashboardPage.jsx or LogsPage.jsx); both do a single fixed-size fetch and the Logs tab only shows "Showing N of M entries" with no way to reach the rest.
- Cited evidence line number for app.js is off (5007-5008 vs actual 5040), minor.

The headline answer (no export exists) is correct and confirmed, but the supporting detail is wrong in ways that would mislead an admin. (a) The entry says both views are "read-only views with paging" — neither has a pager. LogsView requests a fixed limit=300 with no offset control (client/src/pages/LogsPage.jsx:143), and the audit feed has no pager at all. (b) The quoted limits (audit 100 default / 1000 cap; logs 200 default / 1000 cap) are real clamps in audit.js:212,249 and log-store.js:178-197, but they govern the /api/audit and /api/logs APIs, not the Operations Console. The console's Live activity feed is served by /api/admin/dashboard (DashboardPage.jsx:78), whose query is a hardcoded `FROM audit_log a ORDER BY a.id DESC LIMIT 80` (server/app.js:1930-1936). Framing 100/200 as "limits that matter when reading them" sends an admin looking for rows the UI never shows. (c) "Clear log" is on the Logs tab only, not the audit feed. Correct and verified: no export route or control anywhere in audit.js, log-store.js, DashboardPage.jsx or LogsPage.jsx; RETENTION_DAYS=7 / MAX_ROWS=200000 (log-store.js:33-37); and the ACTION_LABELS gap — report.regen (app.js:5040,5052) and scan.share.slack (logged via the template literal `scan.share.${channel}`, app.js:7460-7538) are both absent from ACTION_LABELS (DashboardPage.jsx:8-29), so labelFor renders them as raw dotted keys.

question: How do I scan a whole row of racks in one go with a video?
reasons: The steps and the outcome do not match the code. In /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/client/src/pages/ScanPage.jsx the VIDEO upload tab hard-disables the multi-rack path: line 1019 `const useMultiRack = false;`, so the file is posted as `image` to `/api/analyze`, whose normalizeImage "extracts the single best frame and analyzes it like a photo" (comment at lines 1014-1018). SCAN > Upload > VIDEO > Analyze Rack therefore produces exactly ONE ordinary rack result — no group, no per-rack strip, no combined 3D. The vestigial multi-rack branch (lines 1073-1098) navigates to /results/:id with no `?group` query, and useGroupView (client/src/hooks/useGroupView.js) only reports isGroup when `?group` is present AND members.length >= 2, so RackTabs would render nothing even if that branch ran. The real video-to-multiple-racks flow is a different entry point the answer never mentions: the "Scanning two racks?" card on the Scan page (ScanPage.jsx:1308-1327) leading to /multi-rack/new (client/src/pages/MultiRackNewPage.jsx), titled "Scan two racks", with a "One video" toggle and a "Build combined view" button — and it is explicitly two racks, not "a whole row": it rejects results with `count < 2` ("Only N rack detected — pan across both racks..."), and RackTabs' own docstring describes a "two-rack scan" pill toggle. The duration evidence is also misattributed: validateMedia is only called from ScanPage.jsx:952 (the single-rack path); MultiRackNewPage never calls it, so "Video is too short/too long" never appears in the multi-rack video flow the answer is describing. Additionally the cited RackTabs snippet is right about the code but its stated line range is off (the map starts at line 30, the 3D button at 48-63, so 30-62 truncates it). Following this entry, a technician would shoot a row pan, upload it under VIDEO, get a single rack back, and conclude the feature is broken.

The cited snippets exist verbatim (client/src/utils/validateMedia.js:3-4 MIN_DURATION 1.0 / MAX_DURATION 120; the two duration error strings around lines 95-108; RackTabs.jsx:30-63), but they do not support the described workflow, and the workflow is wrong.

1) SCAN > Upload > VIDEO does NOT produce a multi-rack group. In client/src/pages/ScanPage.jsx the analyze() handler hard-codes `const useMultiRack = false;` (line 1019) with the comment: "A rack video now goes through /api/analyze, whose normalizeImage extracts the single best frame and analyzes it like a photo. The old multi-rack path (/api/analyze-video) required a tenant ... and was overkill for the common one-rack video." The endpoint is therefore always /api/analyze (line 1035), the `if (useMultiRack && data.groupId)` branch is dead code, and navigation is `navigate(/results/${data.rackId})` with NO ?group param.

2) Without ?group, RackTabs renders nothing. client/src/hooks/useGroupView.js requires groupParam present AND equal to data.group.id AND members.length >= 2; RackTabs.jsx:19 returns null when !isGroup. So the rack pill strip and 3D button never appear from the VIDEO tab — that tab yields one rack from one best frame.

3) The real multi-rack video flow is a separate entry point: the "Scanning two racks?" button on ScanPage (navigates to /multi-rack/new) > "One video" > "Build combined view", which posts to /api/analyze-video (client/src/pages/MultiRackNewPage.jsx:102-118) and then navigates to /results/<first>?group=<groupId>. server/app.js:3641+ splits the video into per-rack best frames and creates the group.

4) The 1s/120s limits and the "Video is too short/too long" strings come from validateMedia, imported ONLY by ScanPage.jsx (line 5, called line 952). MultiRackNewPage never calls it, so the flow the entry is actually about has no client-side duration check. Attaching those messages to the row-scan flow is incorrect.

5) Omitted material caveat: /api/analyze-video returns 401 "Authentication required" without a tenant (server/app.js:3647-3654), so owner accounts cannot use it.

question: How do I see what the live network knows about this rack (the Network view)?
reasons: All five cited evidence lines exist verbatim at the stated locations in /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/client/src/pages/NetdiscoPage.jsx (health pill 433-436, "being prepared" 199-204, "not in Network View" 304, Live/Up/Down/All FilterBtns 355-358, Patch Panel filter 209). But the answer's step 1 is wrong for the navigation path it tells the user to take. NetdiscoInner returns early with `if (embedded) return mainContent;` (line 240); the <HealthPill> is rendered only in the standalone page header (line 256). ResultsPage embeds the Network tab via <NetdiscoContent rackId=... /> (line 4836), so a technician who opens the rack and taps More > Network sees NO "Network View online/offline" pill at all — that pill only appears on the standalone route /results/:rackId/netdisco (App.jsx:328). Two further inaccuracies: (a) the entry says the Network tab is behind "More" in the "rack tab strip" — RackTabs is a separate component for multi-rack scans; More lives in ScanTabBar (MORE_TABS = network, drift, ScanTabBar.jsx:13-16), the bottom scan tab bar, and only on non-desktop (ResultsPage.jsx:4323). (b) "Network view is being prepared" does not mean "no discovery server has been set up for your organization": it is set whenever the match fetch fails or returns non-JSON (netdisco_reachable:false), and Netdisco is configured deployment-wide by NETDISCO_URL/NETDISCO_USER/NETDISCO_PASSWORD env vars in server/netdisco_proxy.js (lines 37-39) — there is no per-organization discovery server. Also note the KB already has two entries on these exact banners ("The Network view says 'Network view is being prepared' and never loads." and "The Network View shows \"Network View offline\"...").

Two of the answer's claims fail against source, and the failing one is the very first step a phone technician would take.

1) The "Network View online / offline" pill does NOT exist on the phone path the answer tells the user to take. In /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/client/src/pages/NetdiscoPage.jsx, NetdiscoInner does `if (embedded) return mainContent;` (line ~245) — the <header> containing <HealthPill health={health} /> (line 256) is only rendered in the non-embedded branch. The rack tab strip route uses the embedded form: ScanTabBar's MORE_TABS contains { key: 'network', label: 'Network' } (client/src/components/ScanTabBar.jsx:13-16), which calls handleTabChange, and ResultsPage.jsx:4834-4837 renders <NetdiscoContent rackId={...} />, i.e. NetdiscoInner ... embedded (NetdiscoPage.jsx:56-58). So step 1 ("Check the pill at the top right") is impossible to follow on a phone — the audience the entry is written for. The pill only appears on the standalone route /results/:rackId/netdisco (App.jsx:328 → RackNetworkRoute → NetdiscoPage), which is what the desktop sidebar "Network" link opens (DesktopShell.jsx:273).

2) The stated meaning of "Network view is being prepared" is wrong. The banner renders whenever match.netdisco_reachable === false, which is set on ANY fetch failure or non-JSON body (NetdiscoPage.jsx:118,126) and by the server when the Netdisco call throws (server/netdisco_proxy.js:390-400). That means the discovery server is down, timing out, or misaddressed — not specifically "never set up". It is also not per-organization: Netdisco is a single deployment-wide target configured by NETDISCO_URL / NETDISCO_USER / NETDISCO_PASSWORD env vars (netdisco_proxy.js:37-39), so "no discovery server has been set up for your organization" is factually misleading and invents a per-tenant setting that does not exist.

Correct parts: the Patch Panel filter (NetdiscoPage.jsx:209,228), the disabled "not in Network View" rows (NetdiscoPage.jsx:304 plus `disabled={!live}` on nvRow), and the Live/Up/Down/All filter buttons with counts (NetdiscoPage.jsx:355-358).

Duplication: existing KB entries already cover both banner states in more accurate detail — index 61 ("The Network view says 'Network view is being prepared' and never loads") and index 176 ("The Network View shows 'Network View offline'"). Navigation (More → Network) is covered by index 132.

question: The AR / 3D rack view doesn't work on my Android phone.
reasons:
Both cited snippets exist verbatim (client/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml lines 37-40; notes/artifacts/status-Android.html ~108-112), but neither supports the customer-facing claim, and the shipped code contradicts it.

1) No ARCore in the build. client/android/app/build.gradle has no ARCore / Play-Services-AR dependency. The only Java source is client/android/app/src/main/java/com/racktrack/app/MainActivity.java, a 6-line bare BridgeActivity — no native AR activity, and no `RackAR` Capacitor plugin (grep for "RackAR" across client/src and client/android returns nothing, despite README.md:42 claiming one). The manifest declares no com.google.ar.core meta-data and no `<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.camera.ar">`.

2) The cited manifest line is just a comment plus `<uses-feature android:glEsVersion="0x00030000" android:required="false" />`. A GLES-3.0 not-required flag is evidence about installability only — it does not show an ARCore overlay exists or how to enable it. The comment is aspirational, matching the aspirational README line.

3) The only 3D feature that actually ships is client/src/components/MiniRack3D.jsx, a Three.js/WebGL view. `@react-three/xr` is listed in client/package.json but never imported: no `navigator.xr`, `immersive-ar`, `ARButton`, `XRButton`, or `createXRStore` anywhere in client/src. There is no AR overlay for a technician to open, on any handset.

4) The second citation is notes/artifacts/status-Android.html, an internal build-status artifact whose own text is a to-do ("To keep stable: Note in tester instructions..."). Treating an internal status page as product truth is how this entry inverted reality.

USER lens: it sends a stuck technician to the Play Store to install "Google Play Services for AR" as a fix. That install changes nothing, because the app never requests an AR session — it burns time in a datacenter chasing a feature that does not exist, then says "there is no fix" for the wrong reason. It also implies AR is a shipped RackTrack capability, which will generate repeat tickets.

Near-duplicate too: the verified KB already covers the real question via "How do I see the rack as a diagram or in 3D?" (server/data/support-kb.json, 182 entries).

No corrected answer offered: the true state (AR not shipped; 3D is a WebGL view) is already covered by that existing verified entry, and any rewrite would still answer a symptom I cannot reproduce from source.

Both cited files and line ranges exist and the snippets are verbatim-accurate — but the evidence does not support the claim. The manifest citation is only a code COMMENT mentioning ARCore, and status-Android.html is an internal status/marketing doc, neither of which is implementation. The shipped code has zero ARCore integration: grep for "com.google.ar" across client/android and client/package.json returns nothing; there is no ARCore Gradle dependency in client/android/app/build.gradle; client/android/capacitor.settings.gradle includes only capacitor-android, capacitor-app and capacitor-camera; and the manifest lacks the <meta-data android:name="com.google.ar.core"> entry that every ARCore app is REQUIRED to declare. @react-three/xr is listed in client/package.json line 26 but is never imported anywhere in client/src (no immersive-ar, isSessionSupported, XRButton or createXRStore call exists). The only "AR" present is CSS class naming in client/src/pages/HomePage.module.css (lines 155, 828, 2343, 2413, 2496) for a stylized 2D scan HUD. The actual 3D views — client/src/components/MiniRack3D.jsx, client/src/pages/TopologyScene3D.jsx, client/src/pages/MultiRackTopologyPage.jsx — are plain @react-three/fiber + drei WebGL with OrbitControls, which depend on WebGL/OpenGL ES 3.0, not on ARCore. The answer therefore sends a technician to install "Google Play Services for AR" (a no-op) and then tells them "there is no fix", for a 3D view that never gated on ARCore. The claimed confidence of "certain" is unjustifiable.

question: I'm typing the right password but it keeps saying "Invalid username or password". What's wrong?

The rootCause is broadly correct (single 401 for both 'no user' and 'bad bcrypt compare'; tenantArg switches the string to 'Invalid organization or credentials'), but the entry fails on three counts. (1) DUPLICATE: the existing verified KB already answers this exact question more completely — server/data/support-kb.json line 1598, "Sign-in fails: 'Invalid username or password' or 'Invalid organization or credentials'. What's the Organization box for?" — same symptoms, same rootCause, same evidence snippet, and it additionally covers the Site/tenant match and the deactivated-account message. (2) INVENTED UI DETAIL: the symptom claims a "Red error bar under the password field". .errBox (AuthPages.module.css:281-285) is background #ffffff, border 1px solid #ececec, color #1a1c1d — white with a light-grey border, not red; and it renders after the "Forgot password?" row just above the Sign in button, not under the password field. It also omits the separate 403 "This account has been deactivated. Contact your administrator." path, which is exactly what a user with a genuinely correct password hits. The accurate parts (eye toggle .eyeBtn, "Organization (optional)" label, "Forgot password?" link, 6-digit code from genCode() at auth.js:409, username COLLATE NOCASE, no account-existence leak) do not rescue a lower-quality restatement of a shipped entry plus a fabricated UI description.

The cited evidence is real and the line numbers are accurate (server/auth.js:811 user lookup, :830 the ternary error, client/src/pages/LoginPage.jsx:72 the "Organization (optional)" label, :126 the error box, plus the show/hide password button at :102-108). But the entry fails on two counts.

1) Duplicate. The KB already ships ACCT-016: "Sign-in fails: 'Invalid username or password' or 'Invalid organization or credentials'. question: What does "scan" actually mean in RackTrack? I keep seeing scanning in two different places.
reasons:
The core distinction (photo/CV "scan" vs. network-side SSH/Netdisco reads) is real, but the entry fails verification on both evidence and substance.

EVIDENCE — 2 of 5 citations point at the wrong lines:
1. client/src/pages/ScanPage.jsx "1013-1015" — those lines are the video-upload comment block and `const useMultiRack = false;` (line 1019). The quoted `const endpoint = useMultiRack ...` ternary is actually at lines 1035-1037. Snippet text matches, line range does not.
2. server/app.js "2141-2144" — those lines are the JSDoc for POST /api/detect (the live-overlay YOLO endpoint), not POST /api/analyze. The quoted POST /api/analyze comment is at lines 2173-2176.
The other three citations (client/src/utils/portsProbe.js:1-10, server/netdisco_proxy.js:1-8, netdisco-docker/README.md:4) check out verbatim.

Also note the cited ScanPage snippet is misleading as support for the claim: `useMultiRack` is hard-coded `false` at line 1019, so `/api/analyze-video` is dead code and every photo/video goes through `/api/analyze` (or `/api/analyze-for-ticket`).

SUBSTANCE — the closing claim is factually wrong: "Nothing touches the network" and "you can get a perfect rack scan on a phone with no network access at all." A rack scan uploads the JPEG to the RackTrack server (POST /api/analyze, server/app.js:2173+, which hashes the image, checks outputs/RK-XXXXXXXX/device_unit_map.json, and runs the Python pipeline server-side). question: The Network View header says "Network View offline".
reasons: The cited evidence is genuine and accurately quoted (netdisco_proxy.js:145-161 and :37-40, NetdiscoPage.jsx:429-437 all match verbatim), but the entry fails on two counts. (1) It duplicates an existing verified KB entry: support-kb.json already contains 'The Network View shows "Network View offline" and no discovery data.', which covers the same badge, same root cause, same NETDISCO_URL/USER/PASSWORD guidance, and strictly more (default localhost:5000, the online-but-empty case, the 15 s data timeout, Netdisco's SNMP v2 'public' community). (2) The stated root cause is incorrect: it claims the endpoint reports ok:false when 'no api_key can be obtained'. In netdisco_proxy.js:151 getApiKey() is wrapped in .catch(() => null) and only feeds the 'authenticated' field; 'ok' comes solely from fetch(NETDISCO_URL) (line 153, ok: r.ok || r.status < 500). A credential/login failure therefore leaves ok:true and the badge still reads 'Network View online' — the opposite of what the entry asserts, and precisely the distinction the existing entry documents.

Two disqualifying problems. (1) Factually wrong causal claim: the rootCause says the endpoint "reports ok:false plus authenticated:false when the fetch throws or no api_key can be obtained." In server/netdisco_proxy.js:145-160 the `ok` field is `r.ok || r.status < 500` from an unauthenticated GET of NETDISCO_URL, and the catch sets ok:false. The api_key only populates `authenticated`; it never affects `ok`. NetdiscoPage.jsx:431 keys the badge off `health.ok` alone, so a reachable Netdisco that rejects the login shows "Network View online" with authenticated:false. Consequently the answer's admin remedy — check NETDISCO_USER / NETDISCO_PASSWORD to fix "offline" — is misleading; wrong credentials can never cause that badge. (2) Duplicate: support-kb.json already contains a verified entry "The Network View shows \"Network View offline\" and no discovery data." covering the same failure in more detail, and it explicitly states the correct rule this entry contradicts ("Credentials do not affect the online/offline badge — only the data"). The cited snippets themselves are real and quoted verbatim, and the minor claim that only this screen depends on Netdisco is loose (NetdiscoContent is also embedded in ResultsPage.jsx:4836 and SideBySideRacks.jsx:54), but the contradiction with a shipped entry plus the wrong credential advice is enough to reject.

question: Network View says "Network view is being prepared" and never loads.
reasons:
The user-facing guidance is directionally correct, but two of the entry's technical claims fail verification against source.

1) Bad citation. Evidence #2 cites /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/client/src/pages/NetdiscoPage.jsx lines 259-264 for the "Network view is being prepared." block. Those lines contain the page header/HealthPill markup. The quoted block actually lives at lines 199-204 — a ~60-line miss. (Evidence #1, netdisco_proxy.js 390-400, is accurate: `netdisco_reachable: false` is at line 397 with the `cleaned` message at 394. Evidence #3 is accurate: looksLikeNetdiscoNoise starts at line 25, ending at 40 rather than 39.)

2) Wrong mechanism in the root cause. The entry states looksLikeNetdiscoNoise() suppresses the ECONNREFUSED/traceback text in this scenario. It does not, on this path. When ndGet throws, the proxy returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing netdisco_reachable:false and error:<cleaned>. In fetchMatch (NetdiscoPage.jsx ~100-130) that response is r.ok with parseable JSON, so it takes the `else { setMatch(data) }` branch and looksLikeNetdiscoNoise is never called — the `error` field is simply never rendered anywhere. looksLikeNetdiscoNoise only runs in the !r.ok || !data branch (line 117), i.e. proxy 5xx/empty-body cold start.

Everything else checks out: scheduleNetdiscoSync (netdisco_proxy.js 548-566) does debounce a post-scan push at 1500ms, so "data arrives automatically a moment after the scan" is real; the Devices section renders only the warn block when netdisco_reachable === false.

The three cited snippets exist and are accurate (netdisco_proxy.js ~390-400, NetdiscoPage.jsx 199-204 and 25-39), but the advice built on them is wrong in ways that would strand a technician, and the entry duplicates an existing verified KB entry.

1) "Pull to reload" is fabricated UI. There is no pull-to-refresh anywhere in the client (no `touchmove`, `pullToRefresh`, or refresh handler in client/src), and NetdiscoPage's `fetchMatch()` runs only in a `useEffect` keyed on `[rackId]` (lines 132-136) — there is no polling and no Refresh button on the page. The only way to re-fetch is to leave and re-enter the tab or reload the page. A technician told to "pull to reload" will swipe at a screen that never refreshes.

2) "There is no extra detail to read on screen" is false and is the single most useful diagnostic on the page. The standalone Network View header renders `<HealthPill health={health} />` (line 256), which prints "Network View online" or "Network View offline" (lines 429-438). "Offline" distinguishes "discovery server is down / not configured" from "data not pushed yet" — exactly the distinction the entry says is unavailable.

3) The framing "give it a minute… a brand-new scan genuinely does need a moment" misattributes the banner. The banner is not a "still preparing" state: `netdisco_reachable:false` is set on the ndGet throw path, on `!r.ok || !data` (empty/non-JSON body, 401, 5xx — line 118), and on any fetch rejection (line 126). If no Netdisco/discovery server is configured at all, this banner is permanent. Telling the user to wait implies data is en route when in the common case nothing will ever arrive.

4) The root cause is under-specified: it names only the ndGet-throws path and omits the client-side failure paths at NetdiscoPage.jsx lines 118 and 126.

5) Duplicate: server/data/support-kb.json already contains "The Network view says 'Network view is being prepared' and never loads." (line 2330) with a more accurate answer that names the status pill, the permanence of the banner, and the 15s timeout. This entry is a strictly worse restatement of it.

question: Network View says "No switches detected" even though the rack clearly has switches.
reasons:
Two independent failures.

(1) The core causal claim is wrong. In /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/netdisco_proxy.js the match route pushes EVERY qualifying scan device into `matchedDevices` regardless of whether a Netdisco device was found (`matchedDevices.push({ scanDev: d, cmdbName, nd })`, ~line 449), and serialises them all into `matches` with `netdisco: nd ? {...} : null`. In /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/client/src/pages/NetdiscoPage.jsx the "No switches detected" block (lines 227-232) fires only when `(match.matches || []).filter(m => m.scan.class_name !== 'Patch Panel').length === 0` — i.e. when the scan produced no Switch/Firewall/Gateway/Router device at all (nothing but patch panels, or nothing). Unmatched devices still render, dimmed and non-clickable (`!live` → `nvItemDim`, `disabled`), showing 0 live. So a failure of the three matching strategies produces a dimmed row and "0 live", NOT the "No switches detected" banner. The entry's answer and root cause attribute the message to match failure, which the code contradicts.

(2) The entry also conflates the discovery-server-unreachable case: when Netdisco is unreachable the route returns `netdisco_reachable: false` and the page shows a different banner, "Network view is being prepared." (lines 199-204), never "No switches detected". Advice step 1 ("reload a minute after the scan — the push happens shortly after") targets that case and will not help someone actually seeing "No switches detected".

(3) Evidence citation is off: the second evidence item cites NetdiscoPage.jsx lines 284-292, but the quoted text is at lines 230-231 (only occurrence in the file). The other two citations (netdisco_proxy.js 367-369 for the class filter, and the prefix/IP/name/model chain around 437-450) do check out.

The three-strategy matching description and the patch-panel filter are real (netdisco_proxy.js:367-369, 429-451; NetdiscoPage.jsx:209, 227-233), but the entry's core causal claim is false and it will send a technician down the wrong path.

1. WRONG ROOT CAUSE. "You will see 'No switches detected' when none of those succeed" is not true. The match route pushes EVERY qualifying scan device into `matches`, with `netdisco: null` when no strategy matched (netdisco_proxy.js:472-488). The page renders those unmatched rows anyway, dimmed, labelled "not in Network View" (NetdiscoPage.jsx:305 `nvOff`). The empty state at line 227-233 fires only when `matches.filter(m => m.scan.class_name !== 'Patch Panel').length === 0` — i.e. purely a CLASSIFICATION outcome: the scan found nothing classed Switch/Firewall/Gateway/Router. Matching against the discovery server has no bearing on it. So advice steps 1 and 3 (wait for the push; ask admin about naming) address a condition that cannot produce this message.

2. SYMPTOM LIST CONFLATES TWO DIFFERENT SCREENS. "Devices count shows 0 live" comes from `{match.matched_count} live` (NetdiscoPage.jsx:190) and occurs with rows PRESENT and the empty state ABSENT — it is the matching-failure symptom, the opposite case. Bundling it as a symptom of "No switches detected" is misleading.

3. UI LABEL DOES NOT EXIST. There is no "wrong?" correction on the results screen. The control is a StandardFeedback prompt reading `Detected as <class> — right?` with Yes/No, then a device-type dropdown (ResultsPage.jsx:4763-4774, DEVICE_CLASS_OPTIONS at :99-102).

4. "AND RESCAN" IS WRONG AND COSTLY. /api/feedback/device writes the corrected class straight back into device_unit_map.json (app.js:8189-8199), the exact file the match route reads. Reopening Network View is enough; telling a technician in a datacenter to rescan the rack wastes real time.

Minor: the discovery-server sync is debounced 1.5s after a scan (scheduleNetdiscoSync, netdisco_proxy.js:549-565), so "a minute" is fine as a hedge, but it is irrelevant to this message. Also, an unreachable discovery server shows a different panel ("Network view is being prepared.", line 179-184), not this one — worth stating so the two are not confused.

The quoted docstring lines actually live at 4344 and 4347 (block 4335-4352). The other two ScanPage.jsx citations (1058-1062, 1611-1618) do check out.

When the CMDB rack record sets `verification.mode === 'strict'` (comment at 3456-3457: "Strict mode ... rejects on no_labels_detected"), a label-free photo returns ok:false → HTTP 409, and ScanPage.jsx:981 (`if (vRes.status === 409 || vData.ok === false) setVerifyReject(vData)`) opens the exact same "Wrong rack" modal. 3) Substantive error B — "it asks you to confirm manually instead." In soft mode the server returns ok:true (not ok:null; the docstring quoted as evidence is stale relative to the implementation at 3489-3495), and the client comment at ScanPage.jsx:985-988 says ok:true "covers both the label-match case and the soft-mode no-labels-detected fallback ... Either way, proceed silently." There is no manual-confirm prompt on this path in ScanPage.jsx — grep finds no handling of 'no_labels_detected' or ok===null anywhere in the client. So the unreadable-label case silently proceeds; it does not ask the tech to confirm.

Also imprecise: the comparison is against the CMDB rack record for the ticket's rack_name, and if no CMDB record exists verification passes open ('no_cmdb_record', app.js:3463-3466). The 409 also fires from POST /api/analyze-for-ticket (app.js:4505-4524, `error: 'rack_mismatch'`), not only verify-rack.

The first half is accurate — client/src/pages/ScanPage.jsx:969-993 posts the photo to POST /api/incidents/:inc/verify-rack before the ticket scan, server/app.js:4351-4412 runs analyze + labels OCR and calls verifyRackIdentity() (app.js:3458-3505), and a 409 rack_mismatch renders VerifyRejectModal with the "Wrong rack" badge, "This isn't <expected_rack_name>", and Detected/Expected chip columns (ScanPage.jsx:1600-1645). But the closing paragraph — the part a technician would act on — is wrong on both halves, and it is wrong because the cited evidence is a stale doc comment rather than the implementation. The only verification modal in the page is VerifyRejectModal; there is no manual-confirm modal. The cited snippet "200 {ok:null, reason:'no_labels_detected'} ... UI prompts for manual confirm" (app.js:4347-4349) is an out-of-date header comment — verifyRackIdentity never returns ok:null, so the `verdict.ok === null` message branch at app.js:4414 is dead code. (2) "a hard 'Wrong rack' means it genuinely read labels": not guaranteed. With verification.mode === 'strict' on a rack's CMDB record, a no-labels photo returns ok:false with reason 'no_labels_detected' (app.js:3489), and the client fires the same modal on ANY 409 or ok:false (`if (vRes.status === 409 || vData.ok === false) setVerifyReject(vData)`, ScanPage.jsx:981-984) without inspecting `reason`; the modal even has a dedicated "No labels read" empty state. Telling a tech the block proves labels were read could send them walking to another rack when the real fix is a better photo. Minor extras: verification is skipped for video uploads and when the ticket's rack has no cmdb_racks/<name>.json record (ok:true, reason 'no_cmdb_record', app.js:3461-3464); the only seeded record today is cmdb_racks/RACK-RVEW-CORE-01.json (mode 'soft', min_label_matches 1).

question: A port with a cable plugged in shows as Empty or Unknown. Why?
reasons: The cited constant exists but is never used, so the stated root cause is not true of this codebase. `infer_port_status` (pipeline/port.py:67) and `PORT_STATUS_CONF_MIN = 0.35` (pipeline/port.py:31) are imported once at pipeline/port_pattern.py:42 and never called anywhere in the repo (grep for `infer_port_status` across the tree returns only the docstring at port.py:13, the def, and that import — plus the pending-KB file itself). The shipped status path is entirely different: `classify_ports_by_pattern` (port_pattern.py:414-430) runs a separate status model (port_count.pt) and `_bind_status` (port_pattern.py:142-154) assigns each typed port the status of the status box with the largest IoU >= 0.3; with no overlapping status box, or when the status model returned nothing at all, the port becomes 'unknown'. Code-drawn grid cells use a looser IoU >= 0.20 plus a centre-inside-box fallback (port_pattern.py:487-509). So "Unknown" means "no status box landed on this port", not "confidence below 35%" — there is no 0.35 gate anywhere in the live path. The answer is also contradicted for the port-detail view the screenshot text comes from: runner.py:755-771 sets `CABLE_CONNECTED_MIN = 0.55` and, when the status isn't connected/empty, runs the cable classifier as a binary tiebreaker ("so the UI never shows 'Unknown' — a real port is always either connected or empty"), which means a cabled port can be reported **Empty** simply because the cable classifier scored under 0.55 — a cause the entry never mentions. The `ports_conf 0.23` claim is also a misread: CONF = 0.23 (port.py:23) is the YOLO detection threshold for finding port boxes at all, not a value that "yields empty". The parts that do check out: the UI strings at ResultsPage.jsx:3539, the LLDP/live-switch-as-ground-truth override at ResultsPage.jsx:3639-3646, and the fact that cable colour/type is only computed for status == 'connected' (runner.py:167-169, 773) while 'empty' ports get a port-type classification instead (runner.py:830-834) — so Unknown ports genuinely show no cable detail, just not for the stated reason. Directionally right, mechanically invented.

The entry's central mechanism is false. Its cited snippets exist textually (pipeline/port.py:31 defines PORT_STATUS_CONF_MIN = 0.35; pipeline/port.py:67-70 has that early return in infer_port_status), but infer_port_status is DEAD CODE: a repo-wide grep finds it only in port.py's own docstring/definition and in the import list at pipeline/port_pattern.py:42 — it is never called anywhere (the only other hit is this KB entry itself in support-bot/kb/unverified-pending.json). The 35% threshold never executes, so "Unknown means confidence below 35%" is not why any technician ever sees Unknown. What actually produces 'unknown': status comes from the separate status model (port_count.pt) via status_detections() at port_pattern.py:405-411 (run at CONF = 0.23) and is bound to each port by _bind_status() at :143-154 using geometric overlap — best status box at IoU >= 0.3, otherwise 'unknown'; _status_from_name() (:133-139) is pure string matching with no confidence gate. Synthesized grid cells (grid_ports :480-528) use a looser IoU 0.20 then nearest-neighbour status. No status model configured → everything is 'unknown'. Second error: the entry says Unknown is a deliberate refusal to guess on the selected port, but pipeline/runner.py:756-771 does the opposite on exactly that path — when status is not connected/empty it runs the cable classifier and forces 'connected' if conf >= CABLE_CONNECTED_MIN (0.55) else 'empty', commented "so the UI never shows 'Unknown' — a real port is always either connected or empty." Third error: "cable colour and cable type are skipped for these ports" has the wrong cause — cable classification is gated on status == 'connected' (runner.py:773; enrich_cables_on_map :152-156), so Empty ports show no cable detail either, unrelated to any 35% cutoff. Accurate parts: the ResultsPage.jsx statusText line ('Connected'/'Empty'/'Unknown') and the live-neighbour override comment near lines 3636-3646, plus the retake-photo / trust-the-switch advice. But the explanatory core and root cause are fabricated relative to running code, and a confident "35% sure" rule shipped to a customer is exactly the kind of false precision that destroys trust.

question: My rack map has blank or "Unidentified" rows that I can't click on. What are they?
reasons:
The mechanism and cited evidence are real (client/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx:763 HIDDEN_DEVICE_TYPES = {'Empty','Closed Unit','Unidentified'}, used at :801 in isDevicePickable and :4407 in the hero overlay; pipeline/detection.py:964-988 ensure_every_unit_has_device synthesizes class_name 'Unidentified' with confidence 0.0 — cited line range is off by one but the snippet is verbatim). However the answer states things the codebase directly contradicts:

1) It calls all three labels "rack slots where RackTrack could not identify anything." False for Empty and Closed Unit — those are real YOLO classes (detection.py:146 valid-label list; annotation.py:20 '"Empty": orange — YOLO-classified empty slots'; :21 'Closed Unit — red'). The pipeline makes exactly this distinction on purpose: detection.py:957-959 and runner.py:419-421 state the synthetic placeholder is deliberately NOT called 'Empty' because "'Empty' would be a false certainty", and runner.py:91-93 says "reserve 'Empty' for what the model actually classified."

2) "there is nothing to inspect inside them" is contradicted by pipeline/ocr_devices.py:63-87, whose OCR_CLASSES deliberately INCLUDES 'Unidentified' and 'Closed Unit' ("when the CV classifier can't pin down a device, it tends to be the unusual chassis we most need OCR for").

3) Given the symptom "device not in dropdown", the answer is actively misleading: the picker is a whitelist, not a blacklist. ResultsPage.jsx:797-805 — PICKABLE_DEVICE_TYPES = {'Switch','Patch Panel','Router','Gateway','Firewall','PDU'}; Servers, PSUs, UPSes and Storage Units are detected and drawn but are also absent from the dropdown. A technician whose server is missing would be told to retake the photo for no reason.

4) "kept on the rack picture" is imprecise: the client hero overlay hides them (:4407) and the pipeline's 7_rack_all_ports.png hides them too (runner.py:485-493). They survive only in the step-03 annotated device image (annotation.py DEVICE_NAME_COLOR) and in the U-by-U unit report (runner.py:88-93).

5) "blocked by cables, in deep shadow, or cut off at the edge of the frame" is invented causal detail with no basis in source.

The "no way to type the device in" claim does hold: the device-class correction prompt at ResultsPage.jsx:4767 fires off selectedDevice, and hidden types are never selectable (:801).

Citations check out literally (ResultsPage.jsx:763 HIDDEN_DEVICE_TYPES, the 4400-4407 overlay comment, detection.py:974-976 synthetic Unidentified), but the answer's explanation is wrong in ways that would misdirect a technician.

(1) "Those are rack slots where RackTrack could not identify anything" is false for two of the three labels. **Empty** and **Closed Unit** are real trained classes the model positively assigns (ResultsPage.jsx:21 CLASS_CODE 'Empty':'EMP','Closed Unit':'CL'; annotation.py:20-21 "orange — YOLO-classified empty slots", "red"). Only **Unidentified** means nothing was classified — runner.py:90-94 and detection.py:955-960 both note they deliberately refuse to say "Empty" for an unclaimed row precisely because "Empty" is a positive claim. The entry inverts this distinction.

(2) "Unidentified specifically means... no detector produced any class for it at all, even at low confidence" is incomplete and, in the most common confusing case, wrong. runner.py:620-636 **demotes an already-classified device to "Unidentified"** when it is a port-bearing class (Switch / Patch Panel / Firewall / Gateway / Router) but the port detector returns zero ports: `if not detected_ports: dev["class_name"] = "Unidentified"`. So a row the model *did* confidently call a switch can display as Unidentified. That is exactly the case where a technician says "but I can see a switch there", and the entry's stated root cause sends them chasing shadows/cables when the real failure was port detection (bad angle, glare, too far away).

(3) "They are kept on the rack picture" is contradicted by the cited evidence itself: the hero overlay skips them (ResultsPage.jsx:4407) and the pipeline skips them in 7_rack_all_ports.png (runner.py:488-492). They persist in the unit/device report and some annotated device images, not on the main picture.

(4) Given the symptom "device not in dropdown", saying these three are the unselectable ones misleads. isDevicePickable (ResultsPage.jsx:799-805) only offers PICKABLE_DEVICE_TYPES = Switch, Patch Panel, Router, Gateway, Firewall, PDU. Servers, PSUs, UPSes, Storage Units, Modems, Controllers etc. are also absent from the picker despite being real detections — a far more likely reason a technician's device is missing.

The "you cannot type the device in" claim does hold: device-class correction (submitDeviceFeedback, ResultsPage.jsx:2849) requires a selectedDevice, and hidden types can never be selected. Confidence "certain" is not warranted for the rest.

question: How accurate is RackTrack supposed to be? What error rate should I expect?
reasons:

The vision pipeline, mobile capture flow, ServiceNow bridge, and owner dashboard are working end-to-end on a single-tenant deployment."; pipeline/port.py:27-31 defines PORT_STATUS_CONF_MIN = 0.35 and infer_port_status() returns 'unknown' below it (port.py:68); client/src/pages/ResultsPage.jsx:3617-3618 gates the low-confidence cable warning on cable_confidence < 0.5. However the entry's central factual assertion — "There is no measured accuracy, precision or recall number recorded anywhere in the product" — is false, and falsely in the direction that hurts. The product does compute and display an accuracy percentage: server/app.js:1910-1923 tallies is_correct from feedback.jsonl and app.js:2005 emits `accuracy: (fbRight + fbWrong) ? Math.round(fbRight / (fbRight + fbWrong) * 100) : null` as a headline stat on the owner/Operations Console; GET /api/feedback/stats (app.js:8521-8546) returns total/correct/wrong/accuracy plus a by_device_class breakdown; and app.js:1355-1356 exports `total,correct,wrong,accuracy` as CSV. docs/features/build-15-changelog.html:329 lists "feedback accuracy" among the console's headline stats. The entry's core claim and rootCause ("RackTrack does not publish an accuracy figure"; "No accuracy/precision/recall/mAP figure exists in the repository") are contradicted by shipping code. client/src/pages/HomeStudio.jsx:91 renders a hero stat "98% / accuracy", and HomeStudio is the live home page for viewports >=768px (client/src/pages/HomePage.jsx:266 returns <HomeStudio /> from the "/" route); client/src/pages/HomeDesktop.jsx:117 carries the same "98% / Port accuracy". Separately, pipeline/detection.py:139 and :359 both state the device detector is "field-tested at ~99% accuracy", and line 359 uses that figure as the stated justification for disabling the low-confidence retry pass (detect_devices_retry is a no-op). So two accuracy numbers exist in the repo, one of them user-visible. A support agent following this entry would tell a customer no number is published while the customer is looking at "98% accuracy" in the app. The entry's other four evidence items check out exactly: registry.json has all four models at version "baseline" with metrics {} and promoted_ts null; README.md:152 says "Pre-production."; pipeline/port.py:31 PORT_STATUS_CONF_MIN = 0.35 (used at :68 to return 'unknown'); ResultsPage.jsx:3617 warns when cable_confidence < 0.5. question: My MULTI (stitched) scan failed or produced a rack with devices in the wrong place.
reasons: The entry's central mechanism is unreachable in the shipped product. /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/app.js:2504 builds the stitcher command as `args = [script, '--inputs', ...inputPaths, '--output', outputPath]` — it never passes `--strict`, and grep across the repo shows `--strict` appears only in the argparse declaration at pipeline/rack_stitch.py:380. So `stitch_images(..., require_all_seams=False)` (default, pipeline/rack_stitch.py:236), and the `if require_all_seams:` branch at rack_stitch.py:329-336 that returns ok:false with "seam N->M could not be detected (best score X%); retake those shots with more overlap" NEVER fires from the app. Consequently the server never returns 400 kind:'stitch' for an undetected seam, and the user is never shown that message or offered Retake / Proceed anyway for it. What actually happens (rack_stitch.py:313-317, 339): an unaccepted seam is recorded with accepted:false, added to `uncertain`, the slice is pasted uncropped (butted flush) and the job returns ok:true — the scan proceeds straight to results. The client (client/src/pages/ScanPage.jsx:1174-1180) only does `console.warn('[stitch] N uncertain seam(s)')`; there is no user-visible warning at all. So the entry inverts the failure mode: the real complaint is a silent bad stitch, not a blocking error dialog. Secondary errors: (1) the answer tells users to "shoot in order, top to bottom", but the server runs with auto_order=True (no --no-auto-order flag passed), and auto_arrange_images (rack_stitch.py:160-231) infers top→bottom order itself by pairwise overlap scoring — brute force for N<=7, greedy above — so upload order is not what the user must get right; (2) "Proceed anyway" for MULTI just appends skipQualityCheck=1 (ScanPage.jsx:1154), which bypasses the blur/quality gate on the already-stitched image — it has no relationship to seam detection and cannot be "pushing past the stitch warning"; the Retake/Proceed modal only appears for other retryable 400s (quality on the stitched image, or no devices detected). The cited numbers themselves (max_overlap_ratio 0.60, 0.80 for order inference, x_search 12, peak_margin 0.045, accept rule best-minus-median >= peak_margin) do check out, and 2-8 photos is correct (upload.array('images', 8), min 2 at app.js:2531), but a correct root-cause paragraph attached to a user-facing narrative that cannot occur is worse than useless to a technician.

The entry's central user-facing claim is false. server/app.js:2503 builds the stitcher args as [script, '--inputs', ...inputPaths, '--output', outputPath] — it never passes --strict, and pipeline/rack_stitch.py:236 defaults require_all_seams=False (only set from args.strict at :389). Therefore the `if require_all_seams:` failure branch at rack_stitch.py:329-337 is unreachable through /api/stitch: the "seam N->M could not be detected (best score X%); retake those shots with more overlap" message is CLI-only dev-tool behaviour and is never shown to a technician. Undetected seams are instead recorded in `uncertain`, the panorama is butted flush, ok:true is returned, and ScanPage.jsx:1173-1176 only does a console.warn before navigating straight to the results page — no error, no warning, no choice. The Retake / "Proceed anyway" buttons the entry describes (ScanPage.jsx:1538-1545) belong to the `qualityChoice` blur/glare dialog; analyzeMulti({override:true}) at :1152 merely appends skipQualityCheck=1 (consumed at app.js:2603-2607), which has nothing to do with seam detection. So the answer misdirects the user twice: it promises a blocking error they will never see, and it blames duplicated devices on the user having pressed "Proceed anyway" when duplication in fact happens silently on every unaccepted seam. Evidence is also mis-cited: the app.js 400 kind:'stitch' block is at 2555-2563, not the claimed 2523-2531. The numeric parameters in the root cause (max_overlap_ratio 0.60 / 0.80 for order inference, x_search 12, peak_margin 0.045, flush butting -> duplicate detections) are accurate.

question: The switch make and model say "Not detected", or the model number is wrong.
reasons:
The evidence citations themselves all verify: SwitchInformationPage.jsx:618-626 renders the "Not detected" / "Model not detected" / "Vendor not detected" badges as quoted; 192-220 contain switchStableId() (serial > mac > position), userOverrideKey(), loadOverride()/saveOverride() over localStorage with the quoted comment verbatim; pipeline/ocr_devices.py:478-482 emits ocr_conf/match_conf 0.0 with make/model None (and 531-545 derive match_conf from mean OCR line confidence); the user-guide table row at line 701 matches exactly. The localStorage-only limitation is correct — saveIdent() (line 404-410) only calls saveOverride(), there is no server write.

The entry is refuted on a load-bearing instruction. It claims "You can also use this to overwrite a make or model that OCR read incorrectly — the edit control is available even when RackTrack did detect something." Both halves are wrong in the case the question asks about ("the model number is wrong"):
1. The whole Identification section, including the edit button, is gated at line 613 on `(identMissing || identIncomplete || editingIdent || makeIsUserSupplied || modelIsUserSupplied)`. With `identMissing = !effectiveMake && !effectiveModel` (268) and `identIncomplete = !identMissing && (!effectiveMake || !effectiveModel)` (273), when OCR returned BOTH a make and a model all five flags are false, so no Identification section and no edit control renders at all.
2. Even if it did render, the override could not take effect: `effectiveMake = sw.manufacturer || userMake` and `effectiveModel = sw.model_number || userModel` (255-256) — a detected value always wins over the stored user value, and `makeIsUserSupplied = !sw.manufacturer && !!userMake` (257-258) means the "Manual entry" badge can never appear for a field OCR populated.

So a technician told to "correct the wrong model number" would hunt for a control that does not exist. The override mechanism only fills gaps; it cannot correct a wrong reading. (The partial case is fine: if OCR got the vendor but not the model, "Add model" is offered.)

The "Not detected" / "Vendor not detected" / "Model not detected" badges, the "Manual entry" badge, and the localStorage-only persistence (saveOverride, key `racktrack:${field}:${rackId}::s:serial|m:mac|p:position`, no server write anywhere — confirmed by grep: no other component reads/writes a manufacturer override) are all correct. But the answer's handling of the second half of its own question — "or the model number is wrong" — is false in two independent ways, and it states it emphatically ("the edit control is available even when RackTrack did detect something").

1. The Identification block is gated at SwitchInformationPage.jsx:613 on `(identMissing || identIncomplete || editingIdent || makeIsUserSupplied || modelIsUserSupplied)`. With `identMissing = !effectiveMake && !effectiveModel` (line 268) and `identIncomplete = !identMissing && (!effectiveMake || !effectiveModel)` (line 273), and `makeIsUserSupplied = !sw.manufacturer && !!userMake` (line 257), a switch where OCR returned BOTH a make and a model renders no Identification section and no edit button at all. There is no way to reach the editor to correct a wrong-but-present model. (The code comment at 610-612 says "or whenever the user wants to correct what OCR returned", but the implemented condition is either-missing only — an aspirational comment contradicted by the code.)

2. Even if a value were somehow saved, it would be ignored: `effectiveMake = sw.manufacturer || userMake` and `effectiveModel = sw.model_number || userModel` (lines 255-256). The OCR value always wins; the override is a fallback, never an overwrite.

So a technician told "you can overwrite a model OCR read incorrectly" will hunt for a control that does not exist — exactly the wasted-hour failure mode. The rootCause line is also loose in calling the values "written ... under a key derived from serial > mac > position": there is a fourth fallback `n:${sw.name}` (line 202). Minor, but the entry claims confidence "certain".

question: What is each of the three bottom tabs actually for — HOME, SCAN and PROFILE?
reasons: The cited snippets are all real and quoted accurately (client/src/components/BottomNav.jsx lines 13-17 TABS array, lines 24-34 isAuthed guard + handleScanClick shutter hijack; ProfilePage.jsx topbar with logout icon and the `Show all ${scans.length} scans` button), and the SCAN-tab descriptions (Upload/Camera at ScanPage.jsx:1246-1247, SINGLE/MULTI/VIDEO at 1267-1269) and the 5-newest slice (`scans.slice(0, 5)`) check out. But the answer's central mental model of the bar is wrong on a point a technician will hit immediately: the bottom bar is NOT rendered on the HOME route. In client/src/App.jsx the bar only exists where a route opts in via `<ResponsiveLayout withBottomNav>`, and `<Route path="/" element={<HomePage />} />` (line ~215) has no ResponsiveLayout at all. So tapping the HOME tab navigates to the welcome screen and the bottom bar disappears entirely — the user is stranded on HomeLight and has to press "Get Started" to get back to /scan. The entry instead implies the bar persists and that the only times it is absent are "until you are signed in" and "while you have a rack result open". Two further inaccuracies: the profile meta line renders the tenant/organization name (`user?.tenant?.name || 'Sprintpark'`), not "your site"; and the "Show all N scans" button only renders when `scans.length > 5`. Minor omission: if ScanPage has registered a shutter but `canShoot` is false, the SCAN tap does nothing at all (preventDefault fires, shutterFn does not).

Most of the entry checks out (TABS array, `if (!isAuthed) return null`, the SCAN shutter hijack, ProfilePage's identity / Administration / Data Sources / Recent Scans-with-"Show all N scans" sections, sign-out icon top-right), but it is wrong on the point a lost technician actually needs, and wrong on a detail.

1) FACTUAL ERROR — the bottom bar is NOT present on HOME. In /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/client/src/App.jsx the bar only renders where a route is wrapped `<ResponsiveLayout withBottomNav>`; line 229 is `<Route path="/" element={<HomePage />} />` — bare, no layout wrapper, no BottomNav (grep confirms BottomNav is referenced only in App.jsx and its own file). So tapping HOME takes a signed-in technician to the welcome screen and the bottom bar disappears; the HOME tab can never even show as active. The only ways back are the "Get Started" button (which, when signed in, goes to /scan — HomeLight.jsx:18 `navigate(isAuthed ? '/scan' : '/signup')`) or the back gesture. The entry's "The bar does not appear at all until you are signed in" states the only precondition as sign-in and its HOME blurb never warns the bar vanishes — that is precisely the "HOME shows nothing useful / where did my menu go" confusion the entry claims to resolve.

2) "your site and join month" is wrong on both counts. ProfilePage.jsx:133-135 renders `user?.tenant?.name || 'Sprintpark'` — the organization/tenant name, not a site — and formatJoined (lines 11-16) formats `{ year: 'numeric', month: 'short' }`, i.e. month AND year ("Since Mar 2025").

3) Imprecise: the SCAN hijack calls `e.preventDefault()` whenever a shutter is registered but only fires it `if (canShoot)` — so while the viewfinder is still warming up, tapping SCAN does nothing at all (neither shoots nor navigates), which reads as a dead tab.

Also note heavy overlap with the existing KB entry "Where is everything? I can't find my way around the app.", which already states the three tabs and the rack-tab replacement.

question: Someone told me RackTrack has a Specifications page, a Firmware Check and a Port history page, but they're not in any menu. Where are they?
reasons:
The entry's premise is correct but its actual how-to steps are wrong, and they are the part a technician would follow.

CONFIRMED from source:
- /specifications, /firmware, /port-history are routes in client/src/App.jsx (lines 297-302, 331-333), all ProtectedRoute + withBottomNav.
- They are titled in DesktopShell's PAGE_TITLE map (lines 154-157).

The only component in ResultsPage.jsx that renders Hardware & Firmware / Firmware Update / Vendor Specifications is SwitchInfoModal, which is opened solely by `openSwitchInfo` (ResultsPage.jsx:2364) — and `openSwitchInfo` is never called anywhere in client/src (verified by repo-wide grep; the only hit is its own declaration). 2. The real in-app equivalent is the **Switches** tab (ResultsPage.jsx:4841 renders SwitchInfoContent, i.e. the /switch-info page), whose per-switch card has an in-card tab strip: Specifications / Firmware / SFP Advisor (SwitchInformationPage.jsx:693-695). Audience is correctly end-user and no internal detail leaks, but two of the three redirections are wrong or unverifiable, so this must not ship as written.

The root cause is correct (the three routes exist in App.jsx:297-302/331-333, are titled in DesktopShell.jsx:154-157, and no NavLink in client/src points at them — BottomNav TABS are Home/Scan/Profile only, DesktopShell's links array omits them), but the answer's actionable guidance is false in three ways. Its specifications and firmware/CVE status are shown there" — is not true of this codebase: Vendor Specifications and the firmware version check render only inside SwitchInfoModal (ResultsPage.jsx:383, used once at :4266), which is gated on switchInfoOpen, set true only by openSwitchInfo (ResultsPage.jsx:2364) — a function with ZERO call sites anywhere in the file. (3) The closing general rule is wrong: organization members and sites live on /organizations (App.jsx:258), which is full-page with no app chrome and has NO sidebar link — it is reached from ProfilePage (:148) and works on a phone. Only Data Sources and Marketplace are admin sidebar links. Correct parts verified: FirmwarePage.jsx:136 h1 is "Firmware Check", SpecificationsPage.jsx:141 h1 is "Specifications", PortHistoryPage.jsx:238 h1 is "Port history & drift", Drift sits behind the More button in ScanTabBar.jsx (MORE_TABS = Network, Drift) and ResultsPage.jsx:14 imports PortHistoryContent. OrgConsolePage.jsx:309-310 gates that back link on `isOwner` (`{isOwner && (<button className={styles.backLink} ...`). question: I picked two photos and got "Both photos resolved to the same rack — use two different racks."
reasons:
The two evidence citations are real and accurate: client/src/pages/MultiRackNewPage.jsx:74-80 contains exactly the quoted analyzeImage/id1===id2/throw block with that error string, and client/src/hooks/useGroupView.js:8-10 contains the quoted comment verbatim. The error message, the "Scan two racks" screen title (MultiRackNewPage.jsx:130), the two ImageSlot thumbnails (lines 155-158), and the fix steps are all correct.

What is wrong is the stated root cause, which the answer then repeats to the user as fact. server/app.js:498-527 defines the rack id as `computeRackId` = SHA-256 of the org/tenant scope string plus the RAW FILE BYTES (`fs.readFileSync(filePath)`), truncated to `RK-XXXXXXXX`. It is a byte-exact content hash, not a perceptual/visual fingerprint. Two separate photos of the same cabinet, taken a minute apart or from a slightly different angle, have different bytes and therefore produce DIFFERENT rack ids — they would not trigger this error at all. The entry's central reassurance ("two shots of the same cabinet come back as one rack — even if you took them a minute apart, or from a slightly different angle") is the opposite of how the code behaves, and its closing advice ("If they really are two different racks, take a fresh photo of each") is built on that false premise.

The two ways the error can actually fire are: (1) the same image file was picked into both slots (or two byte-identical copies of one file), which is by far the common case; or (2) the confirmed-rack perceptual bypass at server/app.js:2308-2340 — if the org has confirmed racks, `find_confirmed_rack` can map a re-shot photo onto an already-confirmed rack id and /api/analyze returns that id (`buildResponse(matchId, true)`), so two different photos that both match the same confirmed rack collapse to one id. Note that in case (2) the entry's advice to "take a fresh photo of each" does NOT help — a fresh photo still resolves to the same confirmed rack; the bypass is only skipped with forceFresh.

Because the answer teaches an incorrect mental model and gives advice that is ineffective in one of the two real trigger paths, it is refuted rather than merely imprecise. Claimed confidence "certain" is not warranted.

The cited code exists exactly as quoted (client/src/pages/MultiRackNewPage.jsx:74-80 and client/src/hooks/useGroupView.js:8-10), and the UI labels are real ("Scan two racks" header at line 130, "Build combined view" button at line 164, two tappable photo slots labelled "Rack 1"/"Rack 2" with thumbnails at lines 22-52). Steps 1-3 are correct and correctly ordered. But the entry's explanation and its closing advice are wrong, and both would mislead a technician.

The rackId is NOT a visual fingerprint of the rack. server/app.js:513-542 defines it as `RK-` + the first 8 hex chars of SHA-256 over (org scope + "\0" + the raw bytes of the normalized JPEG): "SHA-256 of the file contents, SCOPED TO THE OWNING ORGANISATION". normalizeImage (app.js:504-510) is deterministic for a given input file, so the same file yields the same id and any two genuinely different photos yield different ids. The answer's claim that this fires "even if you took them a minute apart, or from a slightly different angle" is false in the normal case — those are different files, different hashes, and the build would proceed. The overwhelmingly likely real trigger is that the technician picked the same photo file into both slots (e.g. from the camera roll), which is exactly what the entry's advice fails to name.

The one exception the entry does not know about is the opposite of what it says: the confirmed-rack bypass (app.js:2324-2355) perceptually matches a re-shot photo against racks the org has already CONFIRMED and returns that confirmed rack's id. So two different photos collapse to one id ONLY when that rack was previously confirmed, and the thresholds are deliberately strict, so a noticeably different angle falls THROUGH rather than matching. That makes the entry's final instruction — "take a fresh photo of each" — useless for the same-file case and actively wrong for the confirmed case, where a fresh straight-on re-shoot is precisely what re-triggers the bypass and reproduces the error.

Also note the opening sentence "RackTrack decided your two photos are pictures of the same rack" implies a visual comparison of the two photos; no such comparison happens — the two ids simply came back equal. Confidence claimed "certain" is not warranted.

(For the audience check: the corrected answer stays end-user, avoids RK-hash/SHA internals, and does not leak the bypass implementation.)
