question: I get "No spec match for …" or "Couldn't load specs." — is the model wrong?
reasons: Three problems. (1) Evidence line range is wrong: the `No spec match for` fallback in server/app.js is at lines 7110-7118 (specPayloadFromAgent starts at 7110, the template string is at 7117), not 7056-7063 — that range is _bestSuggestion/_modelSimilarity code. It is 7117 in HEAD too, so this is not working-tree drift. (2) The user-facing claim is backwards. client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx:130-150 defines looksLikeBackendNoise, which matches only 'expecting value', 'traceback', 'jsondecode', 'line 1 column', 'http ', 'econnrefused', 'etimedout', 'pipeline.', 'timed out', 'spawn ', 'python exited', 'exit code'. The string "No spec match for \"X Y\". The agent's web fallback may need 'pip install -r requirements.txt' in Agent/Agent_scrap." matches none of those, so line 888 renders it VERBATIM. The entry's claim that the switch card shows this failure as "Couldn't load specs." is therefore false — that friendly fallback appears only for Python tracebacks/timeouts or a missing error field. Line 888 is also the ONLY place either string is rendered in client/src, so the two "surfaces" the answer describes are one surface. (3) Step 2 ("drop marketing words") is wrong for this path: server/app.js always sends `${vendor} ${model}` to the agent, and agent.py:153-158 _extract_model_candidates keeps only tokens containing a digit, so 'Cisco'/'Nexus' are discarded automatically. The cited pipeline/all_vendor.py:104-113 normalize_model is a different code path (the pipeline), so it does not support the claim. Confirmed parts: agent.py:537-544 notfound text is accurate as quoted; Agent/Agent_scrap/cli.py:206-209 sets ok:false for type 'notfound' and emits no `error` key, so the app.js default string is what surfaces — the stated root cause is right; and saveIdent (SwitchInformationPage.jsx:405-424) does clear specs and re-fetch.

Diagnosis is right, but two load-bearing claims are wrong against source.

1) Message mapping is backwards. In client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx:888 the Specifications tab renders `looksLikeBackendNoise(specs?.error) ? 'Couldn’t load specs.' : (specs?.error || 'Couldn’t load specs.')`. looksLikeBackendNoise (lines 130-150) only matches Python-noise tokens ('traceback', 'expecting value', 'timed out', 'spawn ', 'exit code', ...). The server's notfound string (server/app.js:7117 — note the cited 7056-7063 is stale) contains none of those, so on a switch card the technician sees the FULL 'No spec match for "…". The agent's web fallback may need \'pip install -r requirements.txt\' in Agent/Agent_scrap.' verbatim — not "Couldn’t load specs.". "Couldn’t load specs." is the generic string shown for backend noise/no message, i.e. a different failure. On the scan results page the same error appears as "Could not fetch specs: …" inside the "Vendor Specifications" card (ResultsPage.jsx:526), a surface the entry never mentions.

2) The closing remedy is unusable in the most common case. The Identification block is gated on `(identMissing || identIncomplete || editingIdent || makeIsUserSupplied || modelIsUserSupplied)` (line 613), and identMissing/identIncomplete are false when OCR returned BOTH a make and a model. So when OCR read a complete-but-wrong model — exactly the situation that produces "No spec match" — there is no Identification section and no "Edit" button on the card at all. Worse, `effectiveModel = sw.model_number || userModel` (line 256) makes the OCR/CMDB value win over any stored user override, so even a previously-saved correction is ignored whenever a model_number exists. Telling the technician to "use the Identification editor to correct the model" sends them looking for a control that isn't there.

Also weak: evidence #4 (pipeline/all_vendor.py normalize_model) is a different code path from the spec agent, so it doesn't actually support the "drop marketing words" step; and the Agent notfound message (agent.py:537-544) never reaches the UI because cli.py emits ok:false with no `error` key for type 'notfound' (cli.py:206-213), so app.js always substitutes its own default. The step-by-step model-string advice is sound; the UI instructions are not.

question: The spec lookup spins for ages and then says the lookup took too long.
reasons:
The two error strings exist verbatim in server/app.js, but the entry attributes them wrongly and its remedial advice is unsupported.

1) WRONG ERROR STRING FOR THIS SYMPTOM. "Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment." comes from runPipelineModule (server/app.js:6944-6965, PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000). runPipelineModule is called in exactly two request paths: line 6991 (GET /api/specs/vendors — the vendor dropdown list) and line 7172 (pipeline.sfp_recommend, the SFP-advice endpoint). The actual spec lookup (POST /api/specs, lines 7007-7026, plus the OCR-correction resolver at 7073/7080/7088) and the firmware lookup (POST /api/firmware, line 7206) go exclusively through runAgentCli, whose timeout message is "Agent lookup took too long." (line 7327, AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000). A technician doing a spec lookup can never see "Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment." The rootCause's "(90s for the pipeline module path)" likewise mis-assigns the 90s budget to spec/firmware lookups.

2) THE RETRY ADVICE IS UNSUPPORTED. On timeout the child is SIGKILLed (server/app.js:7325-7327) before writing anything, and the client caches only successful responses — client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx:321-323 calls setCached only inside `if (data && data.ok)`, and client/src/utils/scanPrefetch.js:169-172 has no partial-write path. So "anything RackTrack managed to fetch is remembered" and "the second attempt is normally near-instant" are false for the timeout case the entry is about; the retry repeats the full live fetch.

3) DANGLING CROSS-REFERENCE. The answer says 'See the "No spec match" advice', but no entry in the 182-entry /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/data/support-kb.json mentions "no spec match", "spec sheet" or "/api/specs".

4) Every cited line range is off by ~55 lines (claimed 7250-7257 is actually 7305-7312; claimed 6887-6910 is actually 6942-6965; claimed 6942-6945 is actually 6996-6999), though the snippet text is verbatim.

Confirmed-correct parts: the 60s and 90s constants, SIGKILL-on-timeout, the agent's SQLite cache (~1ms) with a ~4s multi-engine web fallback (comments at 6996-6999 and 7302-7311), the "Get specifications" button label (client/src/pages/SpecificationsPage.jsx:209), and that the work is server-side.

The mechanism is roughly right, but three of the entry's user-facing claims are contradicted by the source, and the cited line numbers do not match the file.

1. Wrong error string attributed to spec lookups. /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/app.js: both /api/specs (lines 7018, 7073, 7080, 7088) and /api/firmware (7206) go exclusively through runAgentCli, whose only timeout message is "Agent lookup took too long." (AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000, app.js:7312/7327). The 90s PY_MOD_TIMEOUT_MS path (app.js:6942, message "Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment." at 6961) is reached only by /api/specs/vendors (--list-vendors) and pipeline.sfp_recommend — i.e. the vendor-name dropdown (surfaced as "Vendor list unavailable: …", SpecificationsPage.jsx:189) and the SFP recommender. A spec lookup can never produce that string, so it is a misleading symptom.

2. Step 1's rationale and its retry instruction are both wrong. On timeout the child is SIGKILLed and nothing is written — Agent/Agent_scrap/agent.py:548 calls live_lookup(..., persist=True), which only persists on a successful return, so a model that timed out is NOT "remembered" and the retry is not near-instant for that reason. And "(or reopen the switch card)" does not work: in client/src/pages/SwitchInformationPage.jsx the fetch fires only when specsStatus === 'idle' (lines 353 and 362); after a failure the status is 'error' (line 324/326) and is reset to 'idle' only when the technician edits or clears the make/model (lines 416, 435). Collapsing and re-expanding the card refetches nothing.

3. Step 2 is wrong diagnostics. An unfindable model does not time out: the live web fallback is self-capped at deadline_sec=8.5 (agent.py:546) and returns a "notfound" result, which the server turns into a fast 404 "No spec match for …" (app.js:7117). Timeouts come from load/spawn contention — the comment at app.js:7305-7311 says the 60s budget exists because Scan Results prefetches /api/specs for every unique (vendor, model) in parallel. So "times out twice ⇒ the model can't be found" will send a technician chasing the wrong problem.

Minor: the answer cross-references a "No spec match" KB entry, but no such entry exists in the 182-entry support-kb.json. Evidence line numbers are also all off by ~55-65 lines (cited 7250-7257 / 6887-6910 vs actual 7305-7312 / 6942-6965), though the snippets themselves exist.

Correct and confirmed parts: the "Looking up specs…" spinner text (SwitchInformationPage.jsx:886), the "Get specifications" button label (SpecificationsPage.jsx:209), the "Agent lookup took too long." string reaching the user verbatim (it is not filtered by looksLikeBackendNoise, which only catches "timed out"), server-side execution, per-rack client caching of successful results, and several seconds being normal for a first unknown-model lookup (~4-9s live fallback).

question: Can I delete a single scan from my history, or clear the whole list?
reasons: The core claim (no way to delete a scan) is TRUE and I confirmed it: ProfilePage.jsx rows have only onClick/onKeyDown -> openScan (lines 222-229, verbatim match); there is no swipe/long-press/clear-history control in the file; /api/scans (server/app.js) is a GET-only read of the outputs dir; and the only DELETE routes in the server are /api/orgs/:orgId, /api/orgs/:orgId/members/:memberId (auth.js), connections, lab devices and marketplace — none touch a scan or rack. However the entry fails the evidence lens and contains one fabricated detail: (1) the server/app.js citation is off by 27 lines — the comment block is at 4900-4903 and `app.get('/api/scans', ...)` is at 4904, not 4873-4877; (2) the server/auth.js citation is off by 9 lines — the transaction block is at 1349-1353, not 1340-1344; (3) the answer's claim that a removed member's scan "loses the 'by <name>' credit" describes UI that does not exist — grep for scannedBy/created_by/createdBy in client/src returns nothing, and /api/scans returns no scanner name (rackId, timestamp, counts, image, qualityWarning only). Worse, the real behaviour is the opposite of reassuring: setting rack_owners.created_by = NULL removes the rack from tenantUserRackIds(), so for a plain member the scan disappears from per-user history entirely (it remains visible to owner/org_admin). Newest-first ordering is correct (sort by timestamp descending, app.js ~4971).

The core claim is correct and verifiable: ProfilePage.jsx (client/src/pages/ProfilePage.jsx:221-246) renders each Recent Scans row with only onClick/onKeyDown -> openScan(s.rackId), no swipe, long-press or clear-history control; server/app.js:4904 exposes GET /api/scans read-only; and an exhaustive grep of every app.delete/router.delete in server/ (auth.js, marketplace_routes.js, connection_profiles_routes.js, lab_devices.js) shows no DELETE route for a scan or a rack. Newest-first sorting is also real (app.js sort on `(b.timestamp||'').localeCompare(a.timestamp||'')`). But two specifics are wrong, and one is an invented UI label. (1) "loses the 'by <name>' credit" — no such string or attribution field exists anywhere in the client; grep for created_by / createdBy / scannedBy / ownerName across client/src returns zero hits, and /api/scans never returns a creator name. It is an invented label. (2) "Ask your organization admin. Removal is a server-side, platform-level clean-up" is wrong about who: an org_admin has no capability that removes a scan. The only route that deletes rack ownership rows is DELETE /api/orgs/:orgId (auth.js:1155), gated by requireRole('owner') — RackTrack platform staff only — and it destroys the entire organization, its sites, members and invites, not one scan. (3) The consequence of member removal is also misstated. auth.js:1350 sets rack_owners.created_by = NULL; because a member's history is scoped by tenant.tenantUserRackIds(tenantId, userId) on created_by (app.js:4921), the scan does not merely "lose credit" — it drops out of the member-role history view entirely while remaining on the platform for owner/org_admin. Minor: the app.js evidence citation says lines 4873-4877; the quoted comment block actually begins at 4900.

question: Owner: what actually deletes old scan folders, and how do I run or preview that clean-up?
reasons: The orphan-GC mechanics in the entry check out almost line for line (RK-* regex, 14-day mtime cutoff, findOrphans/pruneOrphans/run, recursive fs.rmSync with force+maxRetries and no archive, CLI flags, POST /api/admin/orphan-gc/run with dryRun defaulting true via `req.body?.dryRun !== false`, _isAdmin/AUDIT_ADMINS empty-list bypass, audit action orphan_gc.run, 24h unref'd setInterval with ORPHAN_GC_APPLY / ORPHAN_GC_RETENTION_DAYS and the orphan_gc.scheduled log with `sampleOrphans` sliced to 5). But the entry's headline sentence and its rootCause make an absolute claim that the codebase contradicts: "Only orphan GC deletes scan folders" / "orphan_gc.js is the only code path that removes outputs/RK-*/ directories". server/app.js deletes rack folders in three other places — line 2431 (`/api/analyze`, deviceCount === 0), line 2440 (`/api/analyze`, unitCount < 3), and line 2677 (the stitched-scan handler, deviceCount === 0) — each doing `fs.rmSync(rackDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` where `rackDir = path.join(outputsDir, rackId)` (outputsDir = PROJECT_ROOT/outputs, app.js:158). Those post-pipeline quality rejections destroy the just-created outputs/RK-*/ folder before returning the 400. So a technician or owner who sees a rack folder vanish immediately after a failed scan would be sent down the wrong path by this entry. Two smaller imprecisions: the folder regex is case-insensitive (`/^RK-[A-F0-9]+$/i`, orphan_gc.js:48), not the case-sensitive form quoted; and both retention overrides use `|| 14`, so 0 (and negatives via the HTTP body's Number()) also fall back to 14, not just non-numeric values. The scheduled sweep is also a bare setInterval — the first run happens 24h after start, not at start.

Directionally right about how orphan GC works, but it fails the evidence lens and overstates one claim. (1) Both app.js line ranges cited are wrong — off by ~25 lines, at HEAD and in the working tree. _isAdmin plus the POST handler are at /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/app.js:2117-2135, not 2092-2103; the scheduled sweep block is at 2145-2163, not 2120-2138. The snippet text is accurate but the anchors are not. (2) "Only orphan GC deletes scan folders" is false: /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/app.js has three other fs.rmSync(rackDir, { recursive: true, force: true }) sites — lines 2431 and 2440 in /api/analyze (post-pipeline quality rejection: deviceCount === 0, unitCount < 3) and line 2677 in the stitched-scan path (deviceCount === 0) — each deleting the just-created outputs/<rackId>/ folder before returning HTTP 400. Orphan GC is the only thing that deletes aged folders, but a reader would wrongly conclude a quality-rejected scan's folder still exists. Minor imprecisions confirmed in /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/lib/orphan_gc.js: the real regex at line 48 is case-insensitive (/^RK-[A-F0-9]+$/i) — the entry quotes the header comment, which omits the i; and the scheduled job is a bare setInterval(...).unref() with no immediate invocation, so the first sweep is 24h after boot, not at start. Everything else checks out: mtime-based retention, ORPHAN_GC_APPLY=1 / ORPHAN_GC_RETENTION_DAYS, dryRun defaulting true via req.body?.dryRun !== false, AUDIT_ADMINS empty-list-allows-all, audit action orphan_gc.run, log event orphan_gc.scheduled with 5 sample rack IDs, and the CLI (dryRun = !args.includes('--apply'), --retention-days N).

question: Internal: is port history & drift scoped per organization like scan history is?
reasons:
The core direction is right but the entry contains a materially false statement and its evidence does not match the file.

CONFIRMED parts: /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/port_history.js does mount a single `router.use('/api/ports', auth.requireAuth);` and none of the GET handlers consult tenant_id/organization_id/role. `listDevices()` in /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/lib/port_history_db.js runs an unfiltered SELECT (the file contains zero occurrences of tenant_id or organization_id), and per-device routes resolve purely by numeric id, 404ing only when the id is absent. app.js:230 does show the member rack gate. toClientView (port_history_db.js:292) does omit host and ssh_port.

REFUTED parts:
1. FALSE CLAIM: "The manual poll endpoint is likewise open to any authenticated user; the only brake is the rate limit and the busy guard." The actual route at port_history.js:170 is `router.post('/api/ports/:deviceId/poll', auth.requireRole('owner', 'org_admin'), safeAsync(...))` — it is role-gated to owner/org_admin, with an in-file comment stating "Any authenticated member could previously force that against any tenant's device." The entry describes the pre-fix state as current. A support agent using this would wrongly tell a customer that any member can force an SSH poll against any device.
2. The evidence array's snippet for "lines 156-162" reproduces the rate-limit/busy block but silently omits the requireRole middleware three lines above it — that omission is what manufactures the false claim.
3. Every cited line range is wrong. `router.use('/api/ports', auth.requireAuth);` is line 42, not 26. /api/ports/devices is 59-61, not 43-45. The overview handler is 63-67, not 48-52. The poll rate-limit block is 175-181, not 156-162. (app.js 226-234 is approximately right; the "Members: only their own Site" comment is at line 230.)
4. The entry also misses the comment block at port_history.js:27-41 documenting this as known, deliberate and tracked follow-up work pending a schema migration — relevant context for an internal-only entry.

Half right, but wrong on the point that one of its own symptoms ("Who can trigger a manual poll") asks about — and wrong in the unsafe direction for an internal entry.

Verified against /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/port_history.js (186 lines), /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/lib/port_history_db.js and /Volumes/Racktrack/dark_mobile/server/app.js:

CONFIRMED: the READ routes are not tenant-scoped. `router.use('/api/ports', auth.requireAuth)` is at line 42 and no handler below consults tenant_id/organization_id. GET /api/ports/devices (lines 59-61) returns `portsDb.listDevices()` unfiltered, and listDevices() (port_history_db.js:191-193) is a plain SELECT over monitored_devices with no tenant predicate. /overview, /events, /:port/events, /:port/history, /:port/timeline all resolve the device with `portsDb.getDevice(Number(req.params.deviceId))` and 404 only when the id does not exist. The contrast with app.param('rackId') (app.js:207-239) is accurate. `toClientView` (port_history_db.js:292-314) does omit host and ssh_port, so "data-visibility, not credential leak" holds for reads.

REFUTED: "The manual poll endpoint is likewise open to any authenticated user; the only brake is the rate limit and the busy guard." It is not. Line 170 reads:

  router.post('/api/ports/:deviceId/poll', auth.requireRole('owner', 'org_admin'), safeAsync(...))

requireRole (auth.js:533-540) wraps requireAuth and 403s any role outside the list, so a plain member gets 403 before the rate limiter is ever reached. There is an explicit comment at lines 167-169 saying this was tightened precisely because "any authenticated member could previously force that against any tenant's device" — the entry was written against the pre-fix code and was never re-verified. The 5/min rate limit (lines 148-165) and the 409 busy guard (line 179) are real but are the second and third brakes, not the only ones.

Every cited line number is also stale (26→42, 43-45→59-61, 48-52→64-67, 156-162→175-181), which is what let the drift go unnoticed. Shipping this as-is tells support staff that any member can force an SSH session into any org's switch, which would trigger an unnecessary sev escalation and misdescribe the current blast radius.
